newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries steady in London, eyes on Philly survey.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries steady in London, eyes on Philly survey.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries in London struggled at steady levels on Thursday as buyers began to dry up amid overbought signals, traders said.
"Pockets of activity are coming from derivatives players, but real investors are going to be reluctant to buy here," said Charles Quigley, vice-president at Chase in London.
At 1015 GMT, the long bond was quoted at 99-05 yielding 6.69 percent, against 99-02 in Tokyo and 99-06 New York close. The two-year note was unchanged at 100-14, yielding 6.006 percent.
After a stream of mostly encouraging U.S. economic data this week, the focus shifted to the Philadelphia Federal Reserve's June survey of business conditions expected at 1400 GMT on Thursday.
Economists said if the survey's reading came in around the consensus forecast of 7.3 against 1.6 in May, it would cool the Treasury market's recent ardour.
Dick Howard, senior economist at Bank Julius Baer in London, said the survey was particularly important as it had consistently predicted the slowdown in the U.S. growth rate in the last months.
"I don't think the Philadelphia Fed survey is going to move the market by a point, but it might start to swing the sentiment," Howard said.
He said expectations that the Federal Reserve would hold interest rates steady at its July meeting were overdone.
"I would sell the whole curve," Howard said.
He expected the two-year yield to find stiff resistance at 6.0 percent as this level would imply that a Fed tightening was ruled out for the time being, even in August.
Traders said with European spreads narrowing to German Bunds after a recent nervous patch on single currency woes, some investors were shifting out of overheated Treasuries.
The U.S. was also weighed by heavy Eurobond supply and domestic auctions due next week of 2- and 5-year bonds as well as 3- and 6-month bills.
Other data due to be released on Thursday were weekly jobless claims and international trade for April at 1230 GMT, and import/export prices and Q1 current account at 1400 GMT.
The September T-bond futures were quoted unchanged on the day at 112-05 in automated trade.
